A test keeps each entry’s declared access equal to its route layout’s, but a layout that says any leaves the page to its API, and a short named list of entries is deliberately narrower than its layout. The navigation’s hand-written copy is not derived from the map: the product tour’s first step says the sidebar is grouped into Work, Teams, Build, Connect, Knowledge and Admin, while the groups are labelled Home, All teams, Teams and insights, Build, Connect, Knowledge and Admin.
limits.title: A hidden page is not an authorization, and a missing Setup button is not proof of readiness

limits.body: A workflow whose name the catalogue does not know lands under the team’s or Other, and the summary shows structure, not what a particular run will do.
limits.detail: Titles and groups come from a table keyed by template name, so a renamed or custom workflow is listed under its own name in the team or Other section. The recently-run section is the three templates with the latest last-run time among those offered. The summary reads the stored spec: phases come only from nodes that carry a group label, human steps only from nodes whose type starts with human, and conditions, loops and runtime branching are not reflected, so a workflow can ask for a person that the list does not name. Whether a workflow opens a pull request is a text match for pr or pull request in the humanized output and phase names, not a fact about the template. A spec that does not parse shows no summary.
limits.title: Picker groups come from a static table and the process summary is a reading of the spec

limits.body: Files, patches and drafts have ceilings, and a review that may or may not have posted is never re-sent for the person.
limits.detail: The page reads at most 3,000 files in pages of 100, treats any patch over 200,000 characters as absent, and holds a read only for a few minutes and a read holding more than a few million characters of patch is served but not kept, so a very large pull request is read from the host again on the next load. A viewed mark exists only for a file with a patch digest. A person keeps at most 100 drafts per pull request. Only GitHub pull requests with a usable platform credential can be read, and writes need the person’s own saved token on the repository’s approved host. Sending is one POST and one host call with no retry; an unknown outcome blocks another send until the person checks or dismisses it, and the check can answer that it found nothing without proving the review was not posted. A review posts on the head the page showed and is refused if the head moved, so a busy pull request can make a reviewer reload repeatedly. The page only warns when an approval comes from someone who launched or requested the work; whether the platform’s evaluation sets it aside is decided elsewhere.
limits.title: The review page is a GitHub view with bounded reads and a send that cannot be retried

limits.body: Nothing tells a lead a failure is unowned or tells an admin a budget request is waiting; the list is read when someone opens it.
limits.detail: The unowned-failure list is a 30-day window over runs the team owns, so older failures and failures on work shared into the team never appear, and an assignment holds only while its assignee is an active member, after which the run is unowned again. An assignment records who should look; it does not change who launched the run or whose credential it used. A nudge works only for an overdue, pending approval whose Slack announcement was recorded, once per 4 hours per step, and posts a fixed reminder, not a decision. A budget request has a reason and no amount, one may be pending per team, and no code in the route notifies the people who can answer it; saving the cap, even unchanged, closes the pending request. The failure list returns at most 100 rows.
limits.title: A lead’s attention list is a record, not a notification or an obligation

limits.body: They add no authority: datasets are global-only with no add-case route, the Qodo editor can only narrow, and the shell-audit prune deletes only rows of archived templates.
limits.detail: The eval dataset dialog always writes the GLOBAL scope and sets cases only at creation. The PR evaluations list resolves links to pull requests from each repository’s newest 100, so older rows have no link. The Qodo allowlist editor offers only Qodo’s read tools, shows tools the stored list names outside that list as never binding, and never saves an empty list because an empty stored list binds nothing. The shell-audit prune is a preview followed by a confirmed delete of rows older than a chosen number of days whose template is archived; rows of active and draft templates are never deleted, and a real delete writes an audit-log entry. Erasing one Slack user’s channel memory needs the member id typed again to confirm and cannot be undone, and reports how many items were forgotten and restored. Each screen sends the same request an API caller would; the gateway’s role, scope and refusal checks remain the controls.
limits.title: The admin screens added for API-only capabilities expose what the routes allow and no more

limits.body: With the default directory scope every signed-in person sees and can ask to join every active team, and turning on self-service creation hands any organization member team ADMIN over what they create.
limits.detail: The default platform scope shows every active team’s name, description, organization and member count to every signed-in person; teams.directoryScope = organization narrows it, and it is one platform-wide setting, not per organization. The open-request cap, the per-team cooldown (timed from the latest rejection at either step) and the creator cap limit volume, not who may ask: teams.maxCreatedPerUser counts only active teams the person created through self-service, so deactivating one frees a slot, and none of the three applies to an organization ADMIN or platform ADMIN creating a team. A self-service creator becomes team ADMIN, which carries the capabilities to onboard repositories the platform credential can reach and to invite people into the organization (active at once where the organization trusts invites); the setting’s own description says to weigh that. A cross-organization request needs an organization ADMIN’s approval of an organization membership for a person the team has already approved, with the role the team chose. Nothing notifies a requester or a reviewer: no gateway or worker code sends a message about a join request, and reviewers see counts on the team and organization pages. A requester’s message is free text, bounded to 500 characters and shown to reviewers unverified.
limits.title: Join requests and self-service teams are volume limits and an approval step, not a vetting of who may ask

limits.body: The Kata network lock is written for one Kata networking layout, runs its helpers outside the VM and has no profile in the shipped Docker policy broker.
limits.detail: Because every runtime name except runc and runsc-host is treated as Kata, a different runtime (gVisor under another name, a Kata build with another network model) fails at topology detection instead of running unlocked, which is safe but means it is unusable. The holder and the NET_ADMIN helper run under runc on the host kernel; only the workspace and its services run in the VM. Policy changes are verified by reading filter rules back, not by sending traffic, and the boot probe exercises one workspace, not every image or host. Reading the shipped broker policy (containerCreate), a created container may carry no Runtime or one equal to the broker's configured runtime, and must carry no Annotations (add a ref to packages/docker-broker/src/policy.ts at the 'runtime not allowed' check)., while the Kata path starts its helpers with --runtime=runc and its children with CRI annotations; so, as written, the broker would be expected to refuse them, and the combination was not exercised in this review. Whether a disk limit holds under a given Kata runtime was also not verified.
limits.title: Docker Kata support fails closed on unfamiliar topologies and is not shown to pass the policy broker

limits.body: Root, the private-range block and the metadata block are each one environment variable away, and the disk cap is off unless a limit is set.
limits.detail: WORKSPACE_RUN_AS_ROOT, WORKSPACE_BLOCK_PRIVATE_EGRESS and WORKSPACE_BLOCK_METADATA are deploy-time switches, not registry settings, so no admin form or per-run pin changes them. Without WORKSPACE_DISK_LIMIT a workspace container has no storage cap from this platform, and the boot probe checks that Docker accepts the option and which driver reports, not that a write past the limit fails. The baseline is an in-container firewall in the workspace's own network namespace set up by a helper; under runc the workspace still shares the host kernel, and it is the restricted or blocked lock, not the baseline, that confines public destinations. Kubernetes has its own storage limit and security context and does not use these settings.
limits.title: The Docker baseline, user and quota are defaults a deployer can turn off, and they share the host kernel

limits.body: During an open or restricted setup phase, repository-controlled commands hold their declared secrets and workspace proxy credentials with that network access.
limits.detail: Setup steps are shell commands from the saved definition or the base-commit file, so whatever network the setup policy grants is available to them together with the secrets they name. The transition clears and verifies processes, but files, credentials, caches and binaries that setup wrote stay in the workspace the agent then uses; the process check is a keeper-relative sweep, not an inspection of disk state. Attached service containers keep running across the transition in their own containers. The setting does not narrow anything (a stricter setup policy is ignored), is not a per-launch override, and does not apply to shell or container steps.
limits.title: A looser setup phase is a deliberate hole that repository commands and their secrets can use

limits.body: A warning does not stop a write, and a report refreshes its timestamp but not its result.
limits.detail: The write that triggers a warning still happens. The probe runs once per worker start: later refreshes only update the report time, so a daemon or kernel change after boot is not reflected until a restart. The Kubernetes report is derived from a configuration flag, not a probe at report time. Missing or stale reports (a worker that crashed without deleting its row stays counted for up to 30 minutes) produce either no warning or a stale one, and a deployment with no reporting worker is treated as having nothing to warn about. This is separate from the boot refusal for a GLOBAL restricted policy with no proxy.
limits.title: Egress readiness is advisory and reports the boot-time probe

limits.body: The worker checks the shape of the policy, not that a forbidden pod is actually rejected, and the RuntimeClass rule applies only where it is switched on.
limits.detail: The boot check inspects the policy and binding fields; it does not submit a violating pod to see a denial, so a cluster that lacks the admission feature or has an altered object is judged on those fields alone. The RuntimeClass rule in the policy is skipped when the namespace has no required-runtime-class label, and the worker verifies the class only when K8S_REQUIRE_RUNTIME_CLASS is true, so by default pods use the cluster default runtime. Both checks can be disabled by environment, and a RuntimeClass names a handler the worker does not itself prove is a VM-based one.
limits.title: The admission and RuntimeClass checks read objects; they do not try to break them

limits.body: Only some workspace creators opt in, and what the agent commits is delivered as written.
limits.detail: The callers that request bundle delivery are the implementation, implementer-session and decomposition activities; other workspace users keep the per-call credential injection in their own workspace. The trusted workspace guards the token and the branch tip, but the commit itself is whatever the agent produced, so content checks (scanners, gates, review) are still what stands between the agent and a bad change. Each git call costs a workspace creation and a bundle copy, and a delivery that finds the remote moved fails instead of merging.
limits.title: Bundle delivery protects the credential and the remote history, not the content of the commit

limits.body: Team secrets inherit the trust of the repository commands that read them.
limits.detail: A secret reaches setup steps and preview commands as secret environment, and those commands come from the saved definition or from a file on the base commit, so anyone who can change either for a granted repository can make a command read the value and send it wherever the setup network phase allows. Write-only responses, name-only audit entries and the reserved-name list reduce accidental exposure; they are not a boundary inside the workspace. The reserved-name rule is a pattern, so a secret whose name is not reserved but still influences a tool is not caught.
limits.title: A grant extends a team secret to everyone who can change that repository's setup or preview

limits.body: Orchestrations are off by default, bounds are frozen at launch, and several protections depend on what the launcher or an MCP server declares.
limits.detail: Bounds (children, concurrent children, writer children, turns, lifetime, default allowlist) are read once at launch and frozen into the workflow, so an edit reaches only later orchestrations; the kill switch stops further spawns but does not stop children already running. Writer scopes are reserved only while a writer is starting or running, so a finished writer's paths are free for a later writer, and the scope check judges changed paths at delivery, not what a child reads. A path scope list is a push-policy check, not a sandbox for the child's workspace. Whether an MCP call needs approval depends on the server's own readOnlyHint, so a server that mislabels a write as read-only runs it without approval. A viewer who cannot reach the attached repository sees withheld orchestrator messages and child results, but the launcher sees what the orchestrator saw. An orchestration with no activity for a fixed idle period and nothing in flight completes by itself.
limits.title: Orchestrated runs are bounded and partly trust-based

limits.body: The policy keeps a plan inside a fixed skeleton; it does not prove the free steps are useful, and a plan expires if left unapproved.
limits.detail: A free region may use only allowlisted steps and agent nodes with fixed inputs, so a generated plan cannot do the effects the denied list names (tracker writes, outcome publication, MCP calls, authored commands), and a plan that needs one is refused rather than approximated. The cost shown at preview is an estimate with fan-out width assumed and unpriced steps listed. A plan that sits unapproved expires, and approval refuses a plan whose agents, settings or step catalog changed since it was made: the user generates a new one. Saving a plan as a template is DRAFT only, and a scrubbed plan keeps no body to save. A planned run's pull request is advisory-evaluated and never auto-merged, retry of a planned run is refused, and output-only plans rely on a human review of the delivered output.
limits.title: Run plans are constrained, not verified

limits.body: Campaigns cover npm and Go recipes plus agent-made changes, end at draft pull requests, and verify by convention-based test restoration.
limits.detail: The recipe catalogue is code-owned (an npm dependency raised in the root package.json and lockfile, or a Go module in go.mod) and cannot be extended by an admin or a bundle; any other change goes through the agent. The recipe parameters must be an exact version and a registry-shaped name. Verification restores the test files, fixtures, setup files and test-runner configuration that the change touched, recognised by naming convention, so a test outside those conventions, a test setting inside a manifest, the test command and the change's own code are not restored. A campaign opens draft pull requests and never merges, has no CI loop, and its repository list and parallelism are bounded by registry settings resolved at launch. A child cancelled outside the campaign is that target's failure and the campaign carries on.
limits.title: Campaigns are a first slice

limits.body: A macro-built spec is only as editable as its macro, and some paths flatten it.
limits.detail: The runtime ignores uses, so a macro is not a runtime abstraction. The nodes a macro generates cannot be edited without detaching the use (or the spec drifts from its expansion), and the author prompt tells the model to use a macro only when its stock behaviour fits. Refining a generated template shows and returns a flat spec, so a refined template can lose its macro metadata. A generated run plan is judged on its flat nodes only.
limits.title: Macros are an authoring convenience with limits

limits.body: Retention is off until set, skips runs another feature still needs, and a sweep may leave a backlog for later sweeps.
limits.detail: Nothing is deleted while the setting is 0. A run whose artifact backend this process is not configured for can only be kept, so a sweeping process without the object store or filesystem root keeps those runs. A sweep stops at its run, batch and time limits (or on an error) and reports how many it kept by reason, so a large backlog takes several scheduled sweeps. Deletion is permanent and cascades to run-owned records; records that merely reference a run lose the reference.
limits.title: Run-history retention keeps what it cannot safely delete

limits.body: The trigger, initiator and re-run link describe a run and are never consulted to allow or deny anything.
limits.detail: Credentials for a run key on the separate launcher field, not on the provenance. Each launch door stamps only what it knows, and an id that does not resolve at run creation is dropped to null, so a run can lack an initiator or a trigger without failing. Runs created before the columns existed have none.
limits.title: Provenance is a record, not an authorization

limits.body: resetVisits zeroes other nodes' visit counters, and lint refuses a self-reset on a bounded node.
limits.detail: A node that lists itself while setting maxVisits could never exhaust and is refused; naming a node that sets no maxVisits is a warning because nothing counts it; naming an unknown node is an error. Inside a fan-out branch the reset touches that branch's sealed counts only. Generated run plans may not use it, since it could lift the plan's own loop bound.
limits.title: resetVisits and maxVisits rules

limits.body: Nothing starts a triage or postmortem until a team wires an endpoint and automation, change events are best effort, and a diagnosis is model output.
limits.detail: The triage reads at most the latest 25 alerts, log entries and notes with cut text, so a long incident is diagnosed from a sample. The agent’s tools cannot change the repository usefully (the checkout is thrown away), but its note goes to a shared incident timeline under the fromEmail user’s name, and the prompt’s instruction to treat incident text as data is not enforced by code beyond fencing the diagnosis when it reaches the implementer. Fix mode produces a draft pull request only and a person merges. A triage cancelled by incident.resolved can leave a note already posted. A change event is sent only for pull requests the platform opened and recorded, carries the pull request title as written, and a failed send is logged, not retried, so PagerDuty’s timeline can lack a merge. A pagerduty_events routing key cannot be used by workflow steps.
limits.title: PagerDuty runs are opt-in, bounded reads and best-effort sends

limits.body: The preset’s signature check rests on an unconfirmed reading of what Snyk signs, and an endpoint without the two match rules starts a run for every snapshot.
limits.detail: The preset’s own description says Snyk documents its digest as of the request body without saying whether it is the raw bytes, and tells operators to check the first delivery. The event type is fixed because Snyk’s real event name is in an unsigned header, so all filtering is by match rules over the signed body; with none, only the cooldown and the daily cap bound the runs. The advisory fields are the sender’s text, bounded in length and alphabet but not verified, and the agent is told to check them against the repository; a repository the advisory does not affect ends with no pull request rather than an assertion that it is safe. The scan inside the template is advisory, so the draft pull request and CI are the checks.
limits.title: The Snyk preset depends on the sender’s signing and on match rules the team writes

limits.body: Only the holdout randomizes runs, and the intervals ignore that tasks repeat.
limits.detail: The holdout assigns only runs whose configured mode is on, so runs a team configured as shadow or off differ from the on arm in more than recall. Configuration, task mix and missing telemetry can differ between arms, the intervals treat runs as independent although repeated tasks may correlate, and the report itself calls the result observational. Merge and gate outcomes exist only for runs with attributed pull requests or recorded gate results, so each arm’s known-outcome denominators can be much smaller than its run count. Shadow recall still pays for an embedding and a vector search per recall. The arm is read from the run at each recall and pinned at creation, so a setting change reaches only new runs.
limits.title: The recall experiment is an observational comparison, not a measured effect

limits.body: The corpus is capped at 50 lessons, scheduled evals do not use it, and recall is exercised for the implementer rather than every agent.
limits.detail: The corpus is a snapshot an admin authors or imports, so it measures whether those lessons help on fixture cases, not whether production memory does. Retrieval is an exact scan over at most 50 embedded rows, the run fails when the corpus or its embedding model changes after launch, and the corpus hash covers content and failure type only. Recall in an eval run feeds the implementer’s prompt and tools; scheduled evals pin both sides off.
limits.title: Eval memory arms use a small fixed corpus and only the implementer path

limits.body: The trial runs the agent’s own commands, passes without team secrets, and a person decides whether to open the pull request.
limits.detail: A draft’s setup steps and gate commands run in a fresh workspace before a person approves them, so they are agent-written commands from repository content running in a container with the trial’s egress, not the widened draft allowlist, and without team secrets; a repository whose setup needs a secret, an internal host or a service the trial cannot start will fail or block and be reviewed by a person. A passing trial shows the commands succeeded once, not that the gates are the right ones. Approval opens the pull request even when the trial failed or was blocked, and the settings saved on the connection still take precedence over the files until they are removed. Rewriting optional-tool presence checks to warnings means a draft can pass a trial in a workspace that lacks a tool the repository’s real environment needs. The widened draft egress needs the worker egress proxy; without it the draft runs on the ordinary allowlist. Team secrets are withheld, but the repository's own setup secrets are not: a draft that names one receives it in its agent-written setup steps during the trial, before a person approves the draft.
limits.title: Onboarding verifies a draft by running it, which is evidence rather than proof

limits.body: It misses weakenings it has no pattern for, has false positives, does not cover every push path, and does not tell the fixer why it blocked.
limits.detail: The analyser compares counts across the whole diff, so a test moved between files nets to zero, and it can mistake a legitimate consolidation or a deleted test for removed code for a weakening; an assertion moved into a helper or a failing test rewritten to expect the wrong value has no pattern. The default is warn, so the change is pushed and only recorded; block is opt-in per team, organization or step because of the false positives. A blocked step fails non-retryably and the fixer is not told why, so where the run goes next is the template’s failure route. REVIEW_FIX sessions and the initial implementation are not in the guarded modes, and the guard reads the committed diff of the session it wraps, not other pushes of the branch.
limits.title: The test-integrity guard is a heuristic over diff text and warns by default

limits.body: Routing decides which pull requests the queue puts in front of a person and in what order; approvals and branch protection are decided elsewhere.
limits.detail: A pull request that routing says needs nobody can still be merged under the host’s own rules, and one it says needs a person is not blocked. Unknown always means a person: no evaluation at the current head, a stale head, evaluation switched off, or an unrecognised risk class all ask. The attention order reads open pull requests only and the review-time report is capped in rows, repositories and evaluations, with a low-sample flag rather than a refusal. Reviewer time uses stored timestamps only, so approval time, time spent reading and idle time after the last round are not measured, and the host’s own ready-for-review instant is approximated by the platform’s evaluation of it.
limits.title: Review routing orders and labels; it does not enforce review

limits.body: Existing profiles keep hooks on, a plugin’s own MCP servers are not loaded, and the hook switch removes known auto-run sources rather than sandboxing scripts.
limits.detail: The hook switch strips hooks, monitors, LSP servers and hooks frontmatter, but scripts and executables the plugin ships are still written, and the model can still be told to run them; it is not a sandbox. Profiles created before the switch stay hooks-on, updates never turn hooks on, and enabling them needs the reviewed version. The harness runs with strict MCP configuration, so a plugin’s .mcp.json servers are stored and listed at most as declared dependencies but never loaded; an ADMIN can instead map a declared HTTP server to an MCP connection, whose tools the worker relays. Marketplace sync only flags newer commits; it needs the host to answer and a rate-limited answer leaves the status as it was. Plugin loading, hooks and team enablement apply to the Claude Code runtime; for other runtimes only projected skills follow the plugin.
limits.title: Plugins are approved content that run in the workspace, with narrower loading than a full marketplace

limits.body: The warning lists platform-wide agents the harness cannot drive; scoped overrides are not checked and the save still succeeds.
limits.detail: Saving workspace.agentRunRuntime or workspace.implementerRuntime as claude-code returns an advisory in the write response naming (up to eight) active global agents that would follow the setting but whose model is not an Anthropic one, since their runs would fail with HARNESS_UNSUPPORTED_MODEL. The check follows the same model chain the worker does, stops at the first row that names a model, and for the implementer setting covers a fixed set of implementer personas because the worker decides by caller, not by inheritance. Team, organization and template overrides are not walked, an agent resolved in a narrower scope fails at run time, and a failure computing the advice never fails the save.
limits.title: Saving claude-code as a runtime setting warns but does not prevent stranded agents

limits.body: A card cannot trigger anything when clicked, and text in a card shows as typed rather than as Slack markup.
limits.detail: Buttons are links, so there is no interactive card action; human-step approvals in Slack use separate blocks with their own buttons. Card text is escaped wholesale, which flattens Slack link syntax and mentions in a model’s result into literal text. The broadcast defuser covers plain model text it is applied to and does not stop a model from writing text that a person finds persuasive; the writer-file rule is a text match over source, blind to an endpoint built from pieces.
limits.title: Slack cards are link-only and escape model prose

limits.body: The catalog decides what a team, organization or platform role may do; repository reach, run visibility and per-person constraints stay separate gates, and a handler that forgets its check is caught by a test, not at run time.
limits.detail: The catalog’s own comments say that reach (team membership, shares, the GitHub gate) and run visibility are separate gates, and that a team a repository is shared with confers no repository capability, so a capability alone never opens a repository or a run. The handler-checked backstop throws only when NODE_ENV is test; elsewhere it logs authz.unchecked and the response goes out, so a route that declared handlerChecked and then skipped the check is not blocked in production. It counts a check only for a capability the route declared and only an allowed decision. A team capability asked with no team names no resource, which only a platform ADMIN satisfies, and a service principal is refused every capability and admitted only through its token scopes. The dashboard hides what a person cannot do and, for a person with no membership in a team (an organization ADMIN), asks the server per team; the server decides every request regardless. The role-comparison check is a tripwire over source text: it does not see a role held in a variable, a filter object built in one place and used in another, or a comparison made through a helper of the caller’s own. The split migration deleted every role-grantee settings grant and every user grant held by a former platform ENGINEER, which operators re-issue as team-role grants. Capability decisions record their authority in audit context, but the dashboard’s audit view and the CSV export show only the credential path, address and request id.
limits.title: A capability says what a role may do, not what a person may reach, and the unchecked-handler backstop only logs in production

limits.body: The analytics read at most 30 days and capped row sets, count only password failures for known addresses, and alert only as a dashboard list and a per-process metric.
limits.detail: The scan is 30 UTC days and cached for 30 seconds; its peak-hour and action-time series read at most 5,000 newest rows each and say when capped, the people list stops at 5,000 people and says it was truncated, and the alerts list shows at most 50 accounts, reading at most 2,000 failure rows for their methods, cached for 10 seconds. Only the password endpoint with an email naming an existing user writes a failure row, so OAuth and magic-link failures and guesses at unknown addresses appear only in a metric, never in the alert list. Per-account recording is limited to 30 failures a minute, so a threshold above the window’s capacity can never fire, which the answer flags. The threshold-crossing counter lives in one process’s memory (10,000 accounts at most, least recently touched dropped first) and resets on restart, so several gateways count separately; nothing is sent to Slack or email. Events are kept for the activity retention window; history from before sign-in events existed appears only through the opt-in backfill, which copies audit rows inside that window and records the method as unknown with no browser or operating system. Action counts are audit-log rows, so an action that writes none is invisible, and a person’s detail page is itself logged as a sensitive read.
limits.title: User analytics are a bounded scan, and failed-sign-in alerts have no delivery channel

limits.body: Approvals are searched on the server over several relations, and the inbox stream notices change by a count and two timestamps, so a rare swap is left to the page’s own refresh.
limits.detail: The text term is a case-insensitive contains match over step title and description, the request’s ticket and description and the repository, which a plain B-tree index cannot serve; it is ANDed beside the visibility filter, so it can only narrow. The inbox stream polls every 3 seconds per open stream (at most 5 per person) with one aggregate over the visible pending steps and emits a change event only when the count or the oldest or newest requestedAt moves. Removing an interior step while adding another whose requestedAt falls inside the existing range, or a visibility change that swaps equal-sized sets with identical bounds, produces no event; the dashboard’s own periodic refresh covers both.
limits.title: Approval search is an unindexed contains match and the live inbox is a signature poll

limits.body: Run and pull request links on a campaign page come from bounded reads, the start dialog lists a bounded set of repositories, and hidden targets are counted but never named.
limits.detail: A campaign page finds each target’s child run by reading at most the first hundred runs of the campaign’s work request, and each draft pull request’s review page by reading at most a hundred pull requests of the team scope with the campaign’s ticket id, so a campaign with more targets than that can show a repository without a run link or a review link, falling back to the host’s own link where it has one. The start dialog reads the first hundred repositories the person can list and filters them in the browser, so a repository beyond that is not offered. The Cancel button’s visibility only mirrors the check the gateway makes, which is the actual boundary. A viewer who reaches only some of a campaign’s repositories sees a count of hidden targets, so two people can read the same campaign differently, and the progress bar counts all of them. The page reflects the database every ten seconds, not a push,.
limits.title: The campaigns page shows what it was able to join, not every link

limits.body: Teammates can watch but not steer or decide, the live stream is capped per person and degrades to polling, and a viewer without repository reach sees withheld text.
limits.detail: Whether the controls show is the gateway’s answer about the launcher, and each action route repeats the check, so the buttons are not the boundary. A service principal’s orchestration is visible only to that principal through the API and to a platform ADMIN, and its emergency stop is a platform-admin capability. The stream carries at most four concurrent connections per person and resumes from a cursor, but a proxy that buffers it, a refusal or forty-five seconds of silence puts the page back on three-second polling, so a page can lag behind the run. An MCP client can start and message an orchestration but cannot attach, approve or end one, so an orchestration started that way still needs the dashboard for any decision it asks for.
limits.title: The orchestration pages are read-only for everyone but the launcher, and live updates are best effort

limits.body: A button expires after fifteen minutes, carries the goal in a signed but readable value, and only starts generation for a linked clicker.
limits.detail: The token is signed, not encrypted, so the goal text is readable to anyone who can read the posted message’s interactive payload, although the click handler’s own logs and replies carry none. A proposal needs a repository the channel resolves (by default the team’s one repository) or one the person’s own message names, and one the person may reach; otherwise the assistant explains and offers nothing. A click that arrives after fifteen minutes, from another person, or from another message is refused, and an unlinked Slack account gets a private prompt to link it. Single use rests on Temporal permitting one generation job per workflow id derived from the token. The review link is posted best effort: a failure to post it is logged and the generation is already running. Nothing in Slack approves the plan or merges anything.
limits.title: The Slack plan button is a convenience, not an approval

modelDescriptions.Account: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.ActiveWorkflow: Engineering-oriented live domain status, branch and cumulative spend ledger.
modelDescriptions.Agent: Versioned scoped agent persona: model or inherited model, prompt, skills, tool keys, optional MCP connection, runtime (mastra, claude-code or pi) and reasoning level.
modelDescriptions.AgentTrace: Tool call, LLM response or activity event with spend, spec-node link, span correlation, owning team/org and, for an in-app assistant turn, the reply it belongs to.
modelDescriptions.AgentTraceDailyUsage: One UTC day of model-call traces summed per team, organization, run, agent, model, node and launcher (calls, errors, tokens, cost, durations); plain columns with no relations, rewritten a whole day at a time by the rollup sweep.
modelDescriptions.AgentTranscript: One activity attempt’s recorded model traffic: its run (cleared, not deleted, when the run goes), assistant reply, node tag, attempt, runtime, agent keys, status (open, complete, truncated, incomplete, abandoned), call count, size and a hash over its parts, owning team and org, and a run-level and a transcript-level legal hold. Written best-effort by the worker’s transcript recorder, read through run-visibility checks, and deleted after retention unless held.
modelDescriptions.AgentTranscriptPart: One ordered, gzipped NDJSON chunk of a transcript, held as a WorkflowArtifact with its sha256, compressed size and record count; it goes with its transcript, and the sweep removes part artifacts left without a row.
modelDescriptions.ApiToken: Hashed long-lived bearer token owned by exactly one user or service principal, with scopes, expiry and revocation.
modelDescriptions.AssistantAction: A change the in-app assistant proposed and the user’s answer; a confirmed row authorizes one request whose method, URL and body match its digest.
modelDescriptions.AssistantConversation: One user’s private conversation with the in-app assistant, driven by one Temporal workflow; closing it revokes its tokens.
modelDescriptions.AssistantMessage: A user message or the assistant’s reply, filled as the turn runs and streamed from the row; a failed reply carries a redacted cause.
modelDescriptions.Automation: A rule owned by a repository or, for a team-target source, a team: when an occurrence of an event source matches its filters, start a template with its options, within a cooldown and a daily cap.
modelDescriptions.AutomationFire: One decision about one occurrence (a run started, or suppressed and why), keyed on its owner (a repository or an @kind/id) so it outlives the automation; every limit is judged on them. Schedule fires and template webhook calls also leave rows here.
modelDescriptions.AutomationPollState: Poll bookkeeping for one Jira filter automation: the lease replicas take turns with, when and for which narrowed JQL its baseline was taken, the last poll, and a fixed error code (never tracker text).
modelDescriptions.AutomationSeenIssue: An issue key, or issue and status pair, a Jira filter automation has already decided or baselined; kept apart from the decision ledger so its prune never makes an issue look new, and never pruned itself.
modelDescriptions.AutonomyDecision: Audit record of publish and human approval/rejection decisions.
modelDescriptions.AutonomyPolicy: Risk-class rules selected by template/team/global fallback.
modelDescriptions.CallbackEndpoint: A team’s registered run-callback receiver: origin, path prefix, events, sealed signing secrets and an ADMIN-only private-network opt-in.
modelDescriptions.Campaign: A set of repositories in one organisation worked by one pinned template, with an optional code-owned recipe, a parallelism limit frozen at launch and a state that settles once every target does.
modelDescriptions.CampaignAttempt: One numbered try at a campaign target: the workflow run it started, the path taken, its verification, outcome and failure reason.
modelDescriptions.CampaignProposal: A repository a campaign discovery found that the launcher may not start work in. Recorded for a person to decide; never started.
modelDescriptions.CampaignTarget: One repository of a campaign: its state, the path taken (recipe, agent or both), the verification result, the draft pull request it opened and a bounded failure reason.
modelDescriptions.ChannelBudgetHold: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.ChannelMonthlyUsage: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.ChannelOpenItem: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.ChannelThreadSession: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.ConfigAuditLog: Before/after change audit for configuration entities.
modelDescriptions.ConfigPermission: Scoped configuration write grant subject to role floors.
modelDescriptions.ConfigSetting: Validated registry value at a configuration scope.
modelDescriptions.Connection: Team-owned typed integration target; repo coordinates or generic config plus an encrypted token and, for mcp connections, an encrypted set of custom request headers. Git repositories can also store a workspace setup definition that overrides the checked-in setup file. A repository’s own nullable columns override the registry for its pull-request evaluation mode and pull-request title format and template (null inherits); a separate bot-approval flag, off by default, is one more switch beneath the deployment-wide ones. Nullable onboarding milestones record successful access testing, the onboarding pull request URL and number, and dismissal of the first-run checklist. List and detail responses derive stack, unresolved-blocker and first-run milestones from stored detection and relation counts; existing connections are migrated as dismissed. The Connections row menu proposes tools and pull request policy files through the onboarding workflow, with available catalog-tool suggestions from detected stacks.
modelDescriptions.ConnectionCredential: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.ConnectionTeamShare: Shares a repository with another team; canLaunch off makes the share view only, so its members see the repository but cannot start new work on it.
modelDescriptions.ContextSnapshot: Captured request context: ticket, knowledge, Figma design and success criteria.
modelDescriptions.DeviceCode: OAuth device-code exchange state: user and client identities, requested scope/resources, expiry, status and polling interval/timestamp.
modelDescriptions.EmbeddingConfig: Singleton embedding model and credential selection; the provider must be openai, google or compatible, and vectors are 1536 wide.
modelDescriptions.EvalCase: Fixture repository and baseline SHA, toolchain stack (node, python, jvm or go, mapped to a pinned image), golden test, quarantine flag and flake-screen state (runs, screened, infrastructure errors).
modelDescriptions.EvalLesson: Dataset-scoped authored or imported lesson corpus with embeddings and source provenance, isolated from production memory.
modelDescriptions.EvalResult: Normalized per-axis score linked to online or offline evaluation and the node that produced it; a scorer that could not score is marked.
modelDescriptions.EvalRun: Candidate versus baseline benchmark execution, each side’s runtime and a summary; INCONCLUSIVE when no case was screened.
modelDescriptions.EventEndpoint: A team’s signed inbound-event URL: verification scheme, JSON pointers for event fields and sealed current and previous secrets.
modelDescriptions.FailureAssignment: A team lead’s hand-off of a failed run, whose launcher left the team, to a current member. One per run; it records who is to look at the failure and never rewrites the run’s launcher, which keys credentials.
modelDescriptions.FigmaConfig: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.GitHubApproverApp: Separate PR-approver GitHub App identity, encrypted signing key and current/retired bot slugs.
modelDescriptions.GitHubConfig: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.GitHubHostCredential: Encrypted PAT and/or GitHub App credentials for one approved non-instance GitHub host family; sent only to that host.
modelDescriptions.GitHubHostWebhookSecret: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.GitHubInstallation: A GitHub App installation, identified by its host and installation id; repositories may point only at an installation on their own host. Its nullable indexed organizationId links an installation to an Organization (deleting the organization sets it null). The link scopes new imports and installation changes, never existing runs. Org admins connect only new installations of the instance App through signed, user-bound state and OAuth installation verification, and can retire their linked rows; platform admins alone unlink, relink or reactivate, with an outside-org repository count. Unlinked installations remain cross-organization. retiredReason marks a webhook retirement, which only a webhook reverses; manual retirement clears it.
modelDescriptions.HarnessProfile: A named, admin-approved Claude Code profile: the git repository it comes from; its versions are immutable.
modelDescriptions.HarnessProfileVersion: One approved, hash-pinned snapshot of a profile (pinned commit, content hash, stored archive) that an Agent version binds and a run pins.
modelDescriptions.HumanApproval: Distinct human response linked to a human step.
modelDescriptions.HumanErrorBaseline: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.HumanStepDailyRollup: Versioned daily human-step aggregates by scope and resolution dimensions: counts, wait-time sums/buckets and timeouts.
modelDescriptions.IssueTrackerConfig: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.JoinRequestNotification: One notification owed for a join request: the event (created, approved, rejected or waiting on the organization), the audience and channel it goes to, a status with its attempt count, next attempt time and a fixed error code, and a hashed set of the recipients already reached. It is written in the same transaction as the request or decision and delivered by the gateway poller; there is at most one per request, event and audience.
modelDescriptions.Jwks: Rotated signing keys for issued JWTs.
modelDescriptions.KnowledgeBase: Git-backed reference source owned through its connection team, with organization visibility, a path/default ref and indexing metadata.
modelDescriptions.KnowledgeBaseChunk: Snapshot-scoped text chunk with heading, content digest and optional model-labelled vector embedding.
modelDescriptions.KnowledgeBaseConfig: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.KnowledgeBaseLink: TEAM, REPO or TEMPLATE attachment with ref/mount overrides, mandatory TEAM defaults or TEMPLATE exclusions.
modelDescriptions.KnowledgeBaseSnapshot: Immutable KB commit/path index with status, file/chunk/byte counts and flagged/skipped file findings.
modelDescriptions.KnowledgeBaseTeamShare: A same-organization team permitted to attach a SHARED knowledge base.
modelDescriptions.KnowledgeItem: Governed knowledge: owner and origin team, organization, optional repository, type, status, visibility, version, producer provenance and evidence.
modelDescriptions.KnowledgeItemEvent: Append-only lifecycle event of a knowledge item: action, actor and version.
modelDescriptions.KnowledgeItemTeamGrant: A team a selected-teams knowledge item is published to.
modelDescriptions.LessonFlag: One reader’s report, with a reason, that a repository lesson is wrong; a queue for its managers, not a recall filter.
modelDescriptions.MarketplaceSource: A tracked Claude Code marketplace repository pinned to a commit; its catalog lists plugins an admin can approve as profiles, and a sweep flags newer commits.
modelDescriptions.MemoryItem: Scoped semantic memory with vector embedding and run/agent lineage.
modelDescriptions.ModelCatalogEntry: Provider/model capability, price and lifecycle metadata, with optional cache-read and cache-write (5-minute, 1-hour) multipliers that fall back to the code table when null.
modelDescriptions.ModelDiscoveryProviderStatus: One row per provider: when discovery last asked, the fixed-string error if it failed, and the time of the last complete listing.
modelDescriptions.ModelSuggestion: A provider-listed model the catalog lacks (NEW) or a priced model a complete listing no longer shows (RETIREMENT_CANDIDATE), unique per provider and model id, with a sticky dismissal; never read by pricing.
modelDescriptions.OauthAccessToken: Stored opaque access token; JWT access tokens are not stored.
modelDescriptions.OauthClient: OAuth client registered by an MCP client through dynamic registration.
modelDescriptions.OauthClientAssertion: Single-use ledger for private-key client assertions.
modelDescriptions.OauthClientResource: Which OAuth clients may request which resources.
modelDescriptions.OauthConsent: Scopes a user granted a client; its update time marks the grant generation.
modelDescriptions.OauthRefreshToken: Hashed refresh token tied to the user and granting session.
modelDescriptions.OauthResource: Protected resource the authorization server issues tokens for.
modelDescriptions.Orchestration: One conversation in which an orchestrator agent starts sub-agent runs: launcher, named team and organisation, an optional repository attached once, the agent allowlist, the fixed MCP connection set, status and the work request that carries its ledger identity.
modelDescriptions.OrchestrationApproval: One non-read-only MCP call by an orchestration's agent that waits for the launcher: tool, connection, a redacted argument digest, a call key unique per orchestration, the decision and its recorded outcome so a retry never runs it twice.
modelDescriptions.OrchestrationChild: One sub-agent run started by an orchestration: its work request and run, agent, reader or writer role, the path scopes a writer may change, status, and the single structured result the orchestrator reads.
modelDescriptions.OrchestrationMessage: The orchestration transcript: launcher, orchestrator and system messages, with kinds for attach requests, approval requests, child results and notices, an optional child target and a JSON payload.
modelDescriptions.Organization: Organization ownership, governance and budget grouping; trustedInvites lets organization-admin and team-lead/admin invites approve accounts while the organization is active.
modelDescriptions.OrganizationMembership: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.OrgMonthlyUsage: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.OutboundDelivery: Run-callback outbox row written with the event it reports; holds the last status code and a fixed error class, never a response body.
modelDescriptions.PackageRegistry: Platform-ADMIN-managed npm upstream (URL, npm scopes, lockfile or open access mode, bearer or basic auth, optional owning team, encrypted write-only token) that the worker’s registry proxy fronts for that team’s workspaces, or every team’s when it has none.
modelDescriptions.PluginEnablement: Records that a team may use an approved plugin; a team-scoped agent can bind it only while the row exists, and a run fails closed without it.
modelDescriptions.PluginMcpMapping: An administrator's binding of one HTTP MCP server a plugin declares to an existing MCP connection; the worker relays that connection's tools to agents bound to the plugin, and deleting the connection removes the mapping.
modelDescriptions.PrEvaluation: Recorded PR/head evaluation: risk, mode, reasons, brief/readiness, approver counts, outcomes and aggregate human-review feedback.
modelDescriptions.PrFileView: A reviewer’s own mark that they have viewed one file of a pull request, unique per user, pull request and path, and removed with either.
modelDescriptions.ProviderCredential: Scoped encrypted LLM provider key and optional API base: required by a compatible provider, and for a built-in provider a proxy base it is tested, listed and called at, through the outbound guard.
modelDescriptions.PrReviewDraft: A reviewer’s own unsent line comment on a pull request, anchored to a line of a file’s new side at a head and counted as current only while the file’s patch digest is unchanged; it leaves the platform only when the reviewer submits a review.
modelDescriptions.PrReviewVisit: When one person last opened a pull request’s review page and at which head, with the first visit kept to measure how long the pull request waited for a reader; unique per user and pull request.
modelDescriptions.PullRequest: SCM pull-request tracking linked to a workflow and connection: OPEN/MERGED/CLOSED state, draft flag, capped title, and open, merge and close times.
modelDescriptions.RepoAccess: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.RepoDependency: Directed repository dependency with source/provenance and contracts.
modelDescriptions.ReportDigestDelivery: One subscription/period/target delivery ledger with status, attempt count, last error and sent timestamp.
modelDescriptions.ReportDigestSubscription: Scoped report-digest configuration: Slack/email targets, email opt-outs, enablement and last scheduled/test delivery metadata.
modelDescriptions.RepoSetupBlocker: Repository setup failure deduplicated by connection, kind and subject, with redacted diagnostics, occurrence count, first/last seen timestamps and workflow identity. Successful setup or manual dismissal resolves it; recurrence reopens it. Remedies are computed rather than stored, and deleting the connection cascades to its blockers.
modelDescriptions.RepoSetupSecret: One repository's named setup credential: encrypted value, nonce, authentication tag and key version, plus a last-four display marker and timestamps. Unique by repository and name, cascade-deleted with the connection; management returns metadata rather than plaintext, and setup decrypts only named entries for command secret environment.
modelDescriptions.ReviewLaunchIntent: Durable source-run/preset automatic-review decision with claim state, attempts, prepared launch identity and a started, skipped or failed outcome.
modelDescriptions.ReviewPreset: Global or team-owned named review configuration: review-kind template, optional reviewer prompt, test-gate choice, enabled state and report/fix action. Names are unique per team or global scope.
modelDescriptions.ReviewPresetAttachment: A preset attached to one workflow template or repository for automatic review; team-scoped presets require a target in the same team.
modelDescriptions.ReviewVerdictDailyRollup: Versioned daily review aggregates by scope, reviewer, severity and approval: verdict/finding counts, category counts and non-verdict rows.
modelDescriptions.RollupBuiltDay: Completion marker for a day and rollup bucket version, recorded with the rebuilt daily aggregates.
modelDescriptions.RollupSweepState: Named rollup sweep watermark and pending dirty days retained for recomputation.
modelDescriptions.RunCallback: The callback one launch asked for, with its URL encrypted; reports only the execution that asked.
modelDescriptions.RunEffect: Record-only row for one external write a run made (git push, tracker sync, MCP write tool, ticket creation): kind, target, outcome and failure class, owned by the run.
modelDescriptions.RunEvidence: Run-linked screenshot, video, trace or log artifact with source, node/attempt identity and optional caption, page URL and dimensions.
modelDescriptions.RunInput: Stored submitted payload and request history, reused by runs: the organization a connection-free launch was gated against, the service principal that requested it, and whether the platform generated its ticket id.
modelDescriptions.RunPlan: A launch-time generated workflow awaiting its owner's decision: the stated goal, the exact spec a run would execute, its policy and cost reports, the agent versions it was made under and an expiry. An approved plan is pinned as the run's spec snapshot; a plan is never executed unapproved.
modelDescriptions.RunSteeringMessage: A message addressed to a running agent run that its loop takes at the next step boundary; delivery is recorded so a retry does not inject it twice.
modelDescriptions.ScannerPattern: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.ScheduledWorkRequest: Standing repository automation mapped to a Temporal schedule.
modelDescriptions.ServicePrincipal: A team-owned machine identity with connection and template allowlists, a daily run limit and an in-flight limit.
modelDescriptions.Session: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.Skill: Scoped reusable prompt fragment; its text mirrors currentRevision, with a verification flag that edits clear, and an optional link to the external source it was imported from.
modelDescriptions.SkillRevision: Immutable version of a skill’s text and description, with content hash, provenance and advisory scan warnings; runs pin one per skill.
modelDescriptions.SkillSource: An external GitHub repository skills are imported from, pinned to one commit, with the newest commit its ref resolved to at the last successful check, that check’s time and error, script mode, scope and a status; deleting it detaches its skills.
modelDescriptions.SlackChannel: Team/org-owned assistant configuration, optional proactivity and budget settings.
modelDescriptions.SlackChannelMember: One Slack user in a private channel as the last sync saw it; grants that channel’s content to a linked team member while fresh.
modelDescriptions.SlackConfig: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.Team: Team-owned resources, configuration and workflow defaults; carries an optional monthly USD cap and alert threshold of its own.
modelDescriptions.TeamBudgetNotice: Marker row recording that a budget alert was sent: one per team, UTC month and level (WARNING or CAP_REACHED), so the same alert is never sent twice.
modelDescriptions.TeamBudgetRequest: A team lead’s request, with a reason, that an admin change the team’s monthly cap. It carries no amount; at most one is pending per team, and saving the cap resolves it.
modelDescriptions.TeamJoinRequest: A user’s request to join a team, with a message and at most one open per user and team; the team’s managers decide it, and a cross-organization request then needs an organization admin’s decision too.
modelDescriptions.TeamMembership: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.TeamSecret: One team's named secret: encrypted value, nonce, authentication tag and key version, plus a last-four display marker and timestamps. Unique by team and name, cascade-deleted with the team; management returns metadata rather than plaintext, and setup decrypts a value only for a repository it is granted to.
modelDescriptions.TeamSecretGrant: Allows one team secret to reach one repository the team owns. Cascade-deleted with either side and dropped when the repository moves teams; without a grant a team secret reaches no repository.
modelDescriptions.ToolCatalogEntry: Admin-written allowlist of pinned tool downloads (per-architecture https URL and SHA-256, archive member, libc, status) that a workspace may install on demand; a revoked row blocks installs everywhere.
modelDescriptions.TranscriptAccessLog: One transcript content read, download link, verification, export, legal-hold change or identified refusal: actor and role, address, user agent, parameters and how a streamed read ended. No foreign keys, so a row outlives what it names; ADMIN-only and pruned after its own retention.
modelDescriptions.TrustedKnowledgeEvidence: Worker-written provenance of a passed quality gate in one execution, the only evidence a learning may cite.
modelDescriptions.User: Platform identity with role, team/org memberships and authentication relations; a recorded GitHub login also records the linked account it was read from. approvedAt and approvalSource record when and how a waiting sign-up was approved: by an admin, or on a first GitHub sign-in by membership of an organization the github.signInAutoApproveOrgs setting lists.
modelDescriptions.UserActivityEvent: First-party record of a signed-in person's refusals, allowlisted sensitive reads and exports, and (when enabled) page views: a route template, method, status, credential path and truncated address, never a URL, body or query string. No relation to User, so a row outlives the person; pruned by a scheduled, switchable sweep after a configurable number of days.
modelDescriptions.Verification: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.WorkerEgressCapability: Per-process worker report of configured proxies and boot-probed network locking, with a refreshed timestamp for deployment readiness and advisory policy-save warnings.
modelDescriptions.WorkflowArtifact: Large blob in PostgreSQL or S3-compatible storage.
modelDescriptions.WorkflowArtifactChunk: An ordered PostgreSQL bytea chunk (up to 1 MiB) belonging to a workflow artifact; deleting the artifact cascades to its chunks.
modelDescriptions.WorkflowDefaults: Schema entity; inspect fields and relationship declarations below.
modelDescriptions.WorkflowHttpCall: Captured outbound HTTP exchange metadata with workflow/node/attempt and spend-owner identity, optional bounded bodies and transcript/tracing references; runId can be absent.
modelDescriptions.WorkflowHumanStep: Pending/resolved human interaction with context, deadline, approver count and the Slack message that announced it.
modelDescriptions.WorkflowOutcomeReference: One external effect per run, node and connection, claimed PENDING before the provider is called and completed DONE with its result.
modelDescriptions.WorkflowRun: One execution: spec/config snapshots, authorized connections, pinned knowledge-base references, review-source/preset lineage, state, cost and outcome analytics; reapCheckedAt records the run reaper’s last still-running check.
modelDescriptions.WorkflowRunDailyRollup: Versioned daily run aggregates by scope and execution dimensions: counts, cost, time saved, duration buckets, PR outcomes and CI-fix/review metrics.
modelDescriptions.WorkflowShellAudit: Who let one container node or authored command run in a template version: node, image, command, network and egress snapshot, written at save, at serving sign-off, by a bundle install or by the built-in sync (no author).
modelDescriptions.WorkflowStep: One node attempt with inputs, outputs, timing and error.
modelDescriptions.WorkflowTemplate: Named reusable workflow definition with optional review kind, input/provider contract and webhook token/signing configuration.
modelDescriptions.WorkflowTemplateVersion: Immutable spec JSON and input schema at a version; generated versions carry review metadata.
modelDescriptions.WorkspaceSetupCache: Dependency-cache artifact identity, repository, byte size and last-used time; the key incorporates team, repository, setup definition, key-file hashes, image and architecture.
