usecases.body: Separate a connection problem from a run that completed but could not update its ticket.
usecases.detail: An administrator can request stored connection checks, supplying a real ticket ID to include tracker access. Someone who may manage the owning team’s repositories (a team LEAD or ADMIN, an organization ADMIN, or a platform ADMIN) can check one repository's platform and personal credentials and default branch separately. A run's terminal tracker notice identifies a classified refusal (including a Jira or Linear ticket outside the operator’s allowed projects) without exposing provider response text. These diagnostics guide configuration or ticket-workflow investigation; they do not repair credentials, retry a tracker write or prove that a full run will succeed.
usecases.title: Diagnose connection and ticket write-back failures

usecases.body: Review a Confluence page against criteria, leave comments, then propose a ticket hierarchy for a person to approve.
usecases.detail: confluence-review-to-tickets is ordinary document-workspace library content. Its source page and target tracker are separate declared connections. Not-ready documents stop after gated comments so the author can edit and restart. A ready document proceeds through checked planning output, bounded human revisions, structure approval and a separate tracker-write policy gate. Malformed output stops the graph; this is not an automatic document-editing or ticket-execution workflow. Whoever reviews the proposed structure is always a person, whatever the autonomy policy allows: approve continues, request changes sends the note back to the planner (a request after the third replan ends the run FAILED), reject ends SUCCESS with nothing created, and 72 hours without an answer ends TIMED_OUT. Both writes are external_write, a class the fallback rules do not name, so unless a policy names it a person approves each.
usecases.title: Review a document before creating engineering tickets

usecases.body: Ask for another review of a completed change without repeating the implementation run.
usecases.detail: Choose an enabled global or source-team preset from a controllable run, or select a review template in Advanced mode. Attach presets to a repository or workflow template to review successful runs automatically. A network review can be complemented by Qodo at the reviewed head or an explicit human decision. Read the linked verdict, verification and optional test results on the review run; a PR review also posts a comment and contributes current-head evaluation evidence. Fix mode can request a guarded PR feedback round or an unpublished same-agent follow-up for a verified stored change, with reasons when it cannot start.
usecases.title: Review a finished workflow or agent run

usecases.body: A developer submits a repository, ticket and description, then receives reviewed code and a PR.
usecases.detail: Default path: ticket and context (a request validation finds nothing actionable in stops here, FAILED) → TDD implementation → app-preview verification (when the repository configures a recipe) → three-persona review → PR → CI fixes → human merge signal → memory. A review or CI loop that runs out of attempts, or a review that repeats the previous round’s findings, also stores a lesson before the run fails, here and in the other engineering templates that wire an exhausted path to a lesson step. Other engineering templates shorten or add approval steps.
usecases.title: Implement a ticket

usecases.body: Run a library agent for an ad-hoc analysis or bounded change without designing a workflow.
usecases.detail: Delivery can be none, branch or draft_pr. No-delivery results are unverified sandbox views. Publishing validates the exported tree in a separate trusted workspace. The agent runs on a harness only when its own runtime says so; Claude Code gets a per-turn proxy token in its container when the worker’s model proxy is configured (the shipped compose files configure it) and the model key itself without it; Pi keeps its key in the worker.
usecases.title: Explore or change a repository with one agent

usecases.body: Use schedules to launch repeatable repository tasks such as dependency updates, documentation upkeep, vulnerability remediation or security triage.
usecases.detail: The dependency-update, security-triage, docs-refresh and vulnerability-remediation templates are library content; schedule rows point at a saved template/version and target repository. docs-refresh runs the implementer under a documentation-maintainer prompt and confines the step to markdown and docs/ through allowedPaths, which accepts a file, a directory by trailing slash or an extension and fails the step before the push on any other path; it opens a draft pull request, or none when nothing changed. vulnerability-remediation is the dependency-update shape with a remediation brief: the request carries the advisory (a ticket, a Jira filter match, an inbound event or a hand launch; it is not a vulnerability discovery feed), the agent makes the smallest dependency change, the vulnerability scan and tests run in warn mode, a draft pull request opens and CI failures are fixed from the logs up to the CI-fix limit; a run that changes nothing ends SUCCESS with no pull request. None of them merges.
usecases.title: Recurring dependency and maintenance work

usecases.body: Plan work per repository, run independent work concurrently and respect dependency order.
usecases.detail: Epic children resolve each repository team’s default template. A repository starts as soon as its own dependencies succeed, and a repository the planner omits still runs, with no dependencies. A failed/timed-out upstream skips downstream repositories; default-template success can require a human merge.
usecases.title: Coordinate a cross-repository epic

usecases.body: Analyze readiness, solicit clarification, decompose epics/stories, review a plan, create tickets and submit work requests.
usecases.detail: The PRD decomposition activity set differs from the simpler product-prd-draft Notion template. Tracker creation is best-effort. Story dependencies in the decomposition should not be assumed to be the epic orchestrator’s execution scheduler.
usecases.title: Turn a PRD into engineering work

usecases.body: Read a page, draft text, optionally run a brand reviewer and append/create content in Notion.
usecases.detail: Document templates route through policy checks and human approval as specified: the Notion draft records an internal_write decision before it appends, which the default policy publishes without approval, while a policy that requires approval holds the draft for a person, and a rejection or a 24-hour timeout ends the run without writing. Publishing appends blocks/text or creates a page; this is not a full collaborative document editor.
usecases.title: Draft and brand-review Notion content

usecases.body: Read a ticket, generate a response, request approval when required and post a public/private comment.
usecases.detail: record is a workspace provider abstraction. The concrete seeded support path is Zendesk. A hubspot connection can read, search, create and update CRM v3 objects through the generic steps, but no seeded template does.
usecases.title: Draft a Zendesk ticket reply

usecases.body: Directly create an issue or ask issueDrafter to structure a brief first.
usecases.detail: Connection config selects Jira or Linear, with a token and optional project default. Input contracts drive the run form and API validation.
usecases.title: Create tracker issues from structured input or a brief

usecases.body: Post a message to a channel from a reusable workflow with approval routing.
usecases.detail: Uses an api_only workspace and slack_workspace connection. Separate from the richer channel assistant subsystem.
usecases.title: Send governed Slack updates

usecases.body: Mention the assistant, continue a thread, ask for a durable task or draft a reusable workflow.
usecases.detail: General and code routes are mediated by workflow code; background children return structured outputs. Optional digests, open-item follow-ups and cross-channel signals expand proactivity.
usecases.title: Work with a Slack-resident teammate

usecases.body: Wait for deployment approval, staging status and production health before declaring a run successful.
usecases.detail: external-approval-gate and staged-deploy-signals model gates, not deployment engines. No built-in deployment or automatic rollback is performed by these graphs.
usecases.title: Gate a release with external signals

usecases.body: Compose agents, MCP tools, conditions, human decisions and allowlisted container contracts.
usecases.detail: SDK bundles move reusable content between deployments. Custom domain behavior needs real connectors, an MCP server or a coded container capability; generic type registration is not implementation.
usecases.title: Build a custom governed automation

usecases.body: Keep auto-swe’s own built-in model price table current through a draft pull request that a person reviews.
usecases.detail: model-catalog-refresh is installed everywhere but runs only when launched or scheduled against a repository holding the catalog file, normally a fork. Before any workspace exists, the listProviderModels step fails if the file is missing and ends the run SUCCESS when the previous refresh’s branch is ahead of the default branch or has an open pull request. It then lists model ids in the worker through GLOBAL credentials, only for providers already in the file, and hands the agent text with no key. The agent edits only the catalog file: allowedPaths compares the committed tree with the session’s starting commit before the push, and checkScope re-asserts the single path before a draft PR opens. Price-list figures reach the agent as a cross-check only, and after the review network approves, a checkPriceListNotes step sends back to the review fix any added or repriced row that differs from the list without a comment saying so, within the same attempt limit. There is no CI loop or approval inside the run; the draft and its cited price sources are the human gate.
usecases.title: Refresh the built-in model catalog

usecases.body: Request two sequential human sign-offs, or two parallel review-network calls in agreement, on a change whose CI already passed.
usecases.detail: four-eyes and consensus-review open the pull request and run CI with a fix loop first (two fix attempts, a third failure fails the run); only then do two humans, or two parallel review-network calls, judge the head commit. In four-eyes a sign-off can approve, reject — which stops the run — or request changes: a change request needs a written note, goes to a fix that is told the note, then CI again with a fresh budget and both gates again, with every round creating new pending steps, and a third change request fails the run. In consensus-review a rejecting reviewer sends the change to a fix, CI again and the consensus again; it allows three consensus attempts. A fix that changes nothing never waits for a CI event: a no-op CI fix spends an attempt and a no-op review fix returns straight to the gate. Different human identities across the two sign-offs remain a process requirement, not an enforced cross-step constraint; parallel review-network calls also do not guarantee different model identities.
usecases.title: Sequential sign-off or consensus on green code

usecases.body: Turn a failed GitHub Actions run into a diagnosis, and optionally a draft pull request into the branch that failed.
usecases.detail: ci-triage-and-fix is seeded library content, started by a CI-failure automation on a repository or by hand with a run id, and run by the ordinary interpreter with the flagship steps; it is not separately exercised end to end here. The default mode only diagnoses and, for a pull request, comments; fix mode adds a draft pull request into the failing branch, labelled by a reproduce-before-and-after check, and where an admin allows it a pull request’s fix can be pushed onto its own branch instead. Workflow files are never changed and nothing is merged.
usecases.title: Diagnose and fix a failing CI run

usecases.body: Read a Jira or Linear issue, draft a page with the content writer, and create it, or rewrite a named page, in Confluence.
usecases.detail: issue-to-confluence-page runs with no repository: its run connection is the issue tracker and the write names a separate confluence connection, both authorized at launch. The write is policy-gated as external_write, a class the fallback rules do not name, so unless a policy names it the decision defaults to human approval; a supplied page version makes a stale update fail rather than overwrite.
usecases.title: Draft a Confluence page from an issue

usecases.body: Launch template or agent runs with a service principal’s token, start them from signed events, and be told how they ended.
usecases.detail: A principal launches within its scopes, allowlists and limits; an alerting or CI system can post signed events to a team endpoint whose automations start a template; and a launch can ask for a signed completion callback instead of polling.
usecases.title: Start and follow runs from another service

usecases.body: Open the assistant panel to ask how something works, how to configure it, or what the current page shows.
usecases.detail: Answers cite the shipped docs and read platform data through the gateway as the asking user, so it sees exactly what they can; it is off unless an ADMIN enables it and does not change anything.
usecases.title: Ask the platform a question in the dashboard

usecases.body: Read the diff beside the risk class, findings and brief, comment on lines, send a review or send the pull request back to the agent.
usecases.detail: Open the pull request from the Pull requests list or from a run, read the brief for intent and a reading order, mark files viewed as you go (a push that changes a file puts it back among the unviewed), draft line comments on added or deleted lines and ranges, then send a comment, an approval or a request for changes, or send it back to the agent with a note. Writing needs your own saved GitHub token for the repository; without one the page still reads. The review lands on GitHub as you, and the platform records it in its audit log as your act.
usecases.title: Review a pull request the platform opened without leaving the dashboard

usecases.body: A team lead opens Manage, assigns an unowned failure to an active member so it reaches their desk, and nudges an overdue approval in its Slack thread.
usecases.detail: Failures whose launcher left the team or was an automation, within the last 30 days and on the team’s own runs, are listed under Manage. Assigning one records the new owner without changing who launched the run, and the failure appears in that person’s needs-you list while they stay on the team. A stalled approval that was announced in Slack can be nudged once every four hours. Neither action decides the failure or answers the approval.
usecases.title: Hand a failure nobody owns to a teammate and nudge a stalled approval

usecases.body: Launch a campaign that applies the same exact-version upgrade to a set of repositories and reviews the resulting draft pull requests.
usecases.detail: Choose the repositories, describe the change, and optionally pick a recipe (an npm package or Go module and an exact target version). Each repository gets its own run that applies the recipe or the agent change, verifies it against the original tests and opens a draft pull request, or ends successfully with nothing when the repository is not affected. The campaign page shows each target's path, verification and failure reason.
usecases.title: Raise one dependency across many repositories

usecases.body: Describe a task to an orchestrator, attach a repository, and let it start reviewers and bounded writers you can steer or cancel.
usecases.detail: The orchestrator can start read-only agents (research, review) and writers with disjoint path scopes that each deliver a branch or draft pull request; you watch the children, message or cancel any of them, approve their MCP writes, and read each child's result as the orchestrator does.
usecases.title: Break a task into reader and writer sub-agents

usecases.body: Type what you want done, review the proposed workflow and its cost estimate, and approve it to start the run.
usecases.detail: The launcher either picks one of the suggested existing templates or has a plan generated around the shipped delivery core, previews every node and the cost estimate, approves it as the owner, and the run starts pinned to exactly that spec. The plan can be saved as a draft template for reuse.
usecases.title: State a goal and approve a generated plan

usecases.body: An organization admin creates a team, links the organization’s GitHub installation and invites its lead, and the lead brings in people, repositories and a budget.
usecases.detail: An organization ADMIN creates the team in the organization (the creator or a named organization member becomes its first ADMIN) and, through the same organization or the team’s own invite route, invites the lead and members straight into it; the invitees are active at once only where the organization trusts invites. The organization admin can connect the instance GitHub App’s installation for the organization so that only its teams import repositories through it. A team lead then sees a setup checklist (another member, a repository owned or shared, a team budget), onboards or imports repositories, and an organization or team admin sets the cap; a lead who cannot set it files a budget request. People outside the team can find it in the directory and ask to join, which a lead approves, with an organization admin’s second approval when the person is outside the organization. None of this makes anyone a platform admin, and launching work still needs membership or a share.
usecases.title: Bring a new team onto the platform
